note: Adapted from the species description of Speculitermes roonwali in Chhotani (1997), originally in English; neither the soldier nor the worker is recorded, only the alate; the pronotal width is OCR-damaged (given as 1.10.15 in the original) and is not recorded; synonymy citations, figure references and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brownish black; postclypeus and mid-dorsal spot pale brown to brown; antennae pale yellow; labrum yellowish brown; pronotum and tergites dark brown, sternites paler; wings brown; legs yellowish white. Head and body surface densely covered with short, fine hairs and with several long setae. Total body length 13.0-14.0 mm with wings, 7.0-8.8 mm without wings. Head subcircular (length to mandible base 0.96-1.0 mm, maximum width including compound eyes 1.20-1.25 mm); Y-shaped suture indistinct; mid-dorsal spot large and circular, diameter 0.17-0.20 mm. Compound eyes circular, medium-sized, diameter 0.30-0.34 mm. Ocelli oval, translucent (long diameter 0.11-0.13 mm, short diameter 0.08-0.11 mm); eye-ocellus distance less than the short diameter, 0.05-0.06 mm. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 2 about half of segment 1, segment 3 slightly shorter than segment 2, segment 4 as long as or slightly larger than segment 3. Postclypeus moderately raised and pilose, about half as long as wide (length 0.24-0.26 mm, width 0.53-0.57 mm). Labrum hemispherical, wider than long (length 0.26-0.28 mm, width 0.46-0.49 mm). Pronotum wider than long, slightly narrower than head including compound eyes (length 0.66-0.75 mm); anterior margin weakly emarginate or nearly straight, without notches; posterior margin rather strongly concave medially; sides strongly narrowed posteriorly. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Wings dirty brown, anterior and posterior margins pilose, with a few cross-veins between the media and radius; membrane glabrous, densely covered with spinules; lengths of fore and hind wings including scales 10.00-10.75 and 9.90-10.20 mm respectively.
